plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: Leafless stems shoot up almost overnight. Each one carries a crown of crimson flowers with long, curling stamens that look like sparks. In parks, temple grounds and the edges of rice paddies, the blooms form glowing red ribbons.
plants.bloomingSeason: September, around the autumn equinox and into early October
plants.location: Japan, in parks, temple gardens and rice-field margins
plants.funFact: The flowers appear before the leaves, which only emerge after the blooms fade. This is why the plant is linked in Japanese tradition with the autumn equinox holiday.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink blooms rise straight from bare ground in damp meadows and woodland edges. They appear just as most flowers are fading. The spring leaves have long since died back, so the flowers stand alone.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn (August to September)
plants.location: Meadows and gardens across temperate Europe
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a true crocus or the source of saffron. It is a member of the lily relatives and contains colchicine, a powerful toxin that is also used in medicine.

plants.name: Cyclamen hederifolium
plants.description: Swept-back pink petals with a darker magenta mark at the base hover above the woodland floor on slender, curved stems. As the flowers fade, marbled silver-green leaves unfurl and carpet the ground through winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Shaded woodlands and gardens in southern Europe and cool-climate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: After pollination, the flower stalk coils like a spring and pulls the seed capsule down toward the soil. This helps the seeds find a place to sprout.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Clouds of lilac-purple, trumpet-shaped flowers cover this feathery-leaved tree. The blooms often appear before the foliage fully returns. When the flowers drop, they leave violet carpets on streets and pavements.
plants.bloomingSeason: September to November in the Southern Hemisphere spring, with peak color usually in October
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and other warm southern-hemisphere cities
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America but was planted widely in Pretoria from the 1800s. The city is now nicknamed the Jacaranda City.
